chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (mercy of God be upon him) said: My father said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Auramah, from al-Ziyad al-Qandi, from al-Daras, from the man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Verily, for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, there is an angel; from the lobe of his ear to his neck is a distance that a fluttering bird would take five hundred years to traverse.
ai.seo_question: What is the size of the angel mentioned in the hadith of al-Tawhid?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq cites this narration to illustrate the vastness of Allah’s creation, employing the metaphor of a bird's flight over five hundred years to describe the distance from an angel's earlobe to its neck. This emphasizes the incomprehensible scale of the celestial realm, reinforcing the theme of divine greatness (Kibriya) and the humility of human perception in the face of such majesty.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 8. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar (RA) said: My father said: al-Husayn ibn alHasan ibn Aban related to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Auramah, o the authority of Ziyad ibn al-Qandi, on the authority of Durust, on the authority of a man that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:
“Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has created an angel who is so huge that it would take a fluttering bird five hundred years to fly from its earlobe to its neck.”
